newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: European bunkers steady, ARA demand improves.
newsitem.headline: European bunkers steady, ARA demand improves.

text.p: European bunker prices changed little on Thursday with most areas quiet, except ARA where demand improved, dealers said.

Rotterdam 380 CST fuel oil was still offered as competitively as $87.50 fob, after the barge market bounced back from a very low early morning deal at $83. Late afternoon barge talk was around $85/$86 ex wharf.

ARA demand improved after three days of near torpor. Some traders said volumes reached around 20,000 tonnes, half of which came from a single shipping company. One large trading house appeared most successful in supplying its requirements.
Hamburg bunkers dipped by $1 a tonne, although supplies remained fairly tight until the end of the week. Demand remained poor.
Mediterranean prices were broadly steady, although gas oil prices dipped in places. Demand in most ports was weak.

Fujairah bunkers were slightly firmer. Levels fixed on Wednesday of around $94 fob were deemed unattainable today. Shipowners were bound to pay at least 50 cents more and a number did so. Suppliers said the competitive levels drew a number of Asian buyers.
